heading: Splitting the question recovered the missing evidence.
scope: We tested what a small retrieval system kept, what it returned, and whether the returned passages covered every part of a question.

requiredText: Complete declared support at 1, 3 and 5 | 5/6 at each cutoff
All six unsupported questions also returned passages.
Both fixed executions returned identical ordered results.
This result demonstrates sensitivity to asking separate questions under a larger selection budget.
The next application should test one release-or-hold decision for a simulated agent-delivered artifact.
Development retrieval results do not establish predictive or business advantage, recursive adaptation or market concentration.

results.label: Coverage check
results.summary: Two runs reproduced the same result. All six unsupported questions also returned passages; retrieving text does not establish that a question can be answered.

results.label: Fixed follow-up
results.measure: with ten passages instead of five
results.summary: Two separate questions recovered complete evidence for discovery and payment commitment. Both runs agreed. The larger reading budget prevents a claim that this method is better.

limits: These are visible development questions over four saved sources. No answers were generated. Predictive advantage, broader entity coverage and the cause of the retrieval ranking remain unmeasured.

next.question: When should an automated exchange be released or held?
next.description: Prepare a simulation for one agent-delivered artifact. Compare flat and relational records of the same dated evidence about authority, verification and prior release.
next.budget: Two compact views and a lossless control. Measure valid releases, unauthorized releases, duplicates, missing decisions and total processing cost. Live settlement is outside this experiment.
